subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the ratios in which (i) the X-axis and (ii) the Y-axis divide the line segment AB joining A(2, −3) and B(3, −6).

mark_split.label: Ratio in which the X-axis divides AB
Ratio in which the Y-axis divides AB

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 21, book p.143. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The question has two named parts of equal weight, so the 1+1 split is one mark per part. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answers checked by finding the actual crossing points. Line AB has slope (−6 + 3)/(3 − 2) = −3, so its equation is y = −3x + 3. It meets the X-axis at (1, 0) and the Y-axis at (0, 3). Dividing A(2, −3) and B(3, −6) in the ratio 1 : (−2) gives ((3 − 4)/(−1), (−6 + 6)/(−1)) = (1, 0); dividing them in the ratio (−2) : 3 gives ((−6 + 6)/1, (12 − 9)/1) = (0, 3). Both crossing points lie outside the segment, which is what the negative signs in the two ratios record.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say the ratio formula for each axis, and what a minus sign in the answer means.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ratio in which the X-axis divides AB
steps.margin_note: First mark. The X-axis is the line y = 0, so the standard ratio −L₁₁ : L₂₂ becomes −y₁ : y₂. A minus sign in the final ratio means the division is external.
steps.memory_tip: For the X-axis use the y-coordinates: the ratio is −y₁ : y₂.
lines: The minus sign means external division.

recall.must_convey: That the X-axis divides AB in the ratio −y₁ : y₂ = 3 : (−6) = 1 : (−2), that is externally in the ratio 1 : 2.

steps.why: Both A and B have negative y-coordinates, so both lie below the X-axis. The axis therefore cannot cut between them, and the external ratio records exactly that.
common_mistakes: Using the x-coordinates for the X-axis, which is the wrong pair.
Dropping the leading minus sign and writing 3 : 6.

steps.label: Ratio in which the Y-axis divides AB
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The Y-axis is the line x = 0, so the same rule now runs on the x-coordinates. Both ratios come out negative, so both divisions are external.
steps.memory_tip: For the Y-axis use the x-coordinates: the ratio is −x₁ : x₂. The other axis, the other coordinate.

recall.must_convey: That the Y-axis divides AB in the ratio −x₁ : x₂ = −2 : 3, that is externally in the ratio 2 : 3.

steps.why: A and B both have positive x-coordinates, so both lie to the right of the Y-axis, and again the axis meets the line AB only outside the segment.
common_mistakes: Writing the answers as 1 : 2 and 2 : 3 with no mention that both are external.
Swapping the two rules and using y-coordinates for the Y-axis.
